objective: Collect the telemetry needed to notice abnormal activity across in-scope components, and analyse what is noticed so that anomalies are assessed rather than merely recorded.
description: Security-relevant logs are collected from in-scope infrastructure, applications, identity systems, and endpoints into a central store with retention at least matching the examination period. Detection rules or thresholds generate alerts, which are routed to a named responder with a defined analysis timeframe. Each alert receives a recorded disposition indicating whether it represents a security event. Log source coverage is measured against the asset inventory rather than against the sources the platform happens to be receiving.

conditions: The in-scope system produces observable activity, which is effectively universal

implementation_guidance: Measure log source coverage against the asset inventory. A monitoring platform cannot alert on a source that never onboarded, and its own source list always looks complete.
Set retention to at least the examination period plus a margin; default retention is the most common silent failure of this control.
Give alerts a named responder and an analysis timeframe. Alert volume without recorded disposition evidences collection, not monitoring.
Distinguish an anomaly from a security event explicitly, so the handoff to CC7.3 evaluation is defined rather than implicit.
Protect log integrity where feasible, so records of an incident cannot be altered by the same access that caused it.
design_considerations: Is coverage defined by the asset inventory?
Is retention at least as long as the examination period?
Is there a named responder and a defined analysis timeframe?
operating_considerations: Did log collection persist across the period, or did sources drop out?
Were alerts analysed within the stated timeframe, with dispositions recorded?
Can the entity show the alert population is unfiltered?

risks.description: Malicious activity occurs in an unmonitored component and is never observed.
Alerts are generated at a volume nobody can process, so detection exists on paper only.

notes: The criteria name no logging technology, retention period, or detection rule set. Retention adequacy is assessed against the entity's own examination period, not against an external benchmark.
